facts.statement: The genus Perudyptes was described by Clarke and colleagues in 2007.
The only known species within the genus is Perudyptes devriesi.
Perudyptes is a basal penguin found in the Middle Eocene Paracas Formation of Peru.
facts.quote: Perudyptes is a basal penguin from the Middle Eocene Paracas Formation of Peru.

facts.statement: The genus name Perudyptes honors the country of Peru.
facts.quote: The genus name Perudyptes is named after the country

facts.statement: The species name devriesi honors Thomas DeVries, a science teacher who worked in Peru.
facts.quote: the species name devriesi Thomas DeVries, a Vashon Island High School science teacher who has long worked in Peru.

facts.statement: Perudyptes devriesi lived approximately 42 million years ago in the Middle Eocene of Peru.
facts.quote: Perudyptes devriesi is a basal penguin from the Middle Eocene (Mustersan, ~42 Ma) Paracas Formation of Peru.

facts.statement: Perudyptes fills a ~20 million year gap between the earliest penguins (~58–61.6 Ma) and later partial skeletons.
facts.quote: This new discovery is able to fill a major phylogenetic and stratigraphic (~20 million year) gap between the earliest fossil penguins (Waimanu manneringi and Muriwaimanu tuatahi, ~58–61.6 Ma) and the next oldest partial skeletons.

facts.statement: Perudyptes had a skull with deep temporal fossae, an elongate narrow beak, and a short mandibular symphysis.
facts.quote: The skull of Perudyptes is characterized by deep temporal fossae and an elongate, narrow beak that differs from other reported stem penguins in its short mandibular symphysis.

facts.statement: The wing skeleton of Perudyptes shows a mix of primitive features seen in Waimanu and derived features shared with later penguins.
facts.quote: The wing skeleton of Perudyptes preserves a combination of plesiomorphic features also observed in the basal penguin Waimanu and derived features shared with more crownward penguins.

facts.statement: Perudyptes belongs to the order Sphenisciformes.
Perudyptes lived between 48.07 and 41.03 million years ago during the Lutetian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Lutetian to Lutetian (48.07 to 41.03 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Perudyptes is classified within the class Aves.
